title: The Stunning Bravery Of The Russell Brand Survivors
text:
The Stunning Bravery Of The Russell Brand Survivors

Content warning: The following includes descriptions of rape, sexual assault and abuse that some readers may find distressing.

Shame has changed sides. For you, me and women survivors everywhere some justice has been served: the comedian Russell Brand, 51, has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for raping a 21-year-old woman and sexually assaulting three other women between 2004 and 2009. In a UK court on November 9th, he was cleared of two further charges of rape and one of attempted indecent assault.  

It’s hard to believe he’s been convicted with a lengthy sentence, isn’t it? It isn’t hard to believe survivors of rape or sexual assault, and yet, as we all know, all too often the blame falls upon the rape or sexual assault victim, not the perpetrator. Data from eight major US cities — from Los Angeles and Chicago to San Francisco — shows that less than 4% of sex crimes result in convictions, according to a study conducted by NBC News. Even though Brand was found guilty, women still feared the famous media personality would be handed a lenient sentence. Fear not; Brand must serve two-thirds of the 10-year and six-month sentence before he will be eligible for parole.  

All of this happened because truly brave women survivors came forward. Over the past four weeks, a jury of eight men and four women has watched, listened and deliberated a verdict, without any CCTV footage or forensic evidence, in Southwark Crown Court. On the day of sentencing, after Brand had been found guilty, these four incredibly brave women shared their victim impact statements (it can play a crucial role in the sentence given for Brand’s convicted crimes against them). From behind a curtain, one survivor, whom Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting, shared: “I wanted to express how this crime has impacted me. I’ve been in shock and turmoil for weeks. I was extremely upset and traumatized. I didn’t have any respect for myself. I was thinking I was damaged goods — scared of giving off signals that could be taken the wrong way […] I just want to say — a leopard may change its spots, but it’s still a leopard.” 

Another survivor, whom Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting in 2005, had her court statement read for her by the prosecution, one part of it read: “Over the years, hearing his [Brand’s] voice on television or seeing his image has made me jump.” In a similar vein, a survivor whom Brand was convicted of anally raping in 2009 said in her court statement read by the prosecution: “I am living with trauma and something I carry every day,” sharing that she had to take time away from work, move back in with her parents and she worried she’d contracted HIV. The final court statement from the fourth victim, whom Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting while working on a Channel 4 project with him in 2009, was also read for her by the prosecution, saying that following the incident she was “really upset” and felt she “lost my trust in people”. “I felt my working environment wasn’t safe,” she says, adding: “I felt powerless in that moment.” Thankfully, they’re all entitled to lifelong anonymity.  

And let’s not forget that Brand’s conviction happened because of truly brave journalists (many of whom are women). In 2023, a joint media investigation carried out by The Times and Channel 4’s Dispatches, aired the documentary Russell Brand: In Plain Sight. It helped to expose sexual misconduct by Brand, and subsequently, women came forward with complaints about the comedian to the police. In other words, it gave women hope. Hope they would be believed. Hope they would be listened to. Hope they will see some sort of justice.  

In his closing remarks, senior crown prosecutor David Roberts said: “Today’s result shows that fame, status, and a passage of time do not change the fundamental issue of consent. He continued by saying Brand is a “manipulative sexual predator, using his growing fame and power to create situations in which he could pursue women sexually, regardless of what they wanted, with complete disregard for the impact of his actions”. He also praised the survivors. When a sexual survivor makes an allegation, they know everything will be scrutinized about them, because for millennia shame has sat with us. Women have always been shamed for men’s wrongdoings. Today, judge Justice Bennathan made it clear shame must change sides by saying: “Whatever women wear. Wherever they go. Indeed, whatever they drink. They retain the right to say ‘no’ and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators — like you, Russell Brand — act without their consent.”  

Brand probably thought he’d be free right now. I did, too. As the Me Too movement showed, some male celebrities are never reprimanded for sexual harassment or rape. Women who feel safe enough to come forward are not believed, silenced, shut down and never see some justice. So, let me say it again for the women who made this happen: Brand has been found guilty and sentenced to more than 10 years in prison — a sentence I never thought I’d get to write. He’s a convicted rapist. But the women who came forward will never feel truly free; they’ve had to endure a prison-like hell of their own for decades after what he did to them. But their bravery has helped shame change sides, just like Gisèle Pelicot. Their bravery will be remembered, and their bravery will help other women come forward and be believed, too.  

If you’ve experienced sexual violence of any kind and need help or support, please visit Rainn or call 800-656-4673.

title: This Is What 2027 Will Smell Like, Based On Your Star Sign
text:
This Is What 2027 Will Smell Like, Based On Your Star Sign

The leaves are changing color, matcha lattes are being enjoyed hot, and sweaters are coming out of retirement. Yes, fall is officially here — and as we enter the -ber months, we can’t help but get a little nostalgic as the year winds down. As any frag-head knows, scent and nostalgia are deeply connected, making this the perfect time to refresh your perfume wardrobe for a new season and an even newer year. (2027, you aren’t ready for us.) 

In the season-one finale of Nose Dive, host Asia Grant sits down with celebrity astrologer and Astrolotea podcast host Aliza Kelly to discuss all things scent and stars, including what 2027 has in store for you, according to your zodiac sign. Think of it as your cosmic guide to finding a fragrance that feels written in the stars.

DashDividers_1_500x100

“Astrology is about embodiment [and] celebrating yourself. It’s about building confidence, knowing what makes you special, and understanding other people,” Kelly says. And what better way to celebrate your unique self than with a signature scent? Grant and Kelly kick things off with the fire signs — Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius — and the notes that best capture their bold, passionate energy. “This is giving something that’s pretty, spicy, and warm,” says Grant, who gravitates toward notes like incense, leather, and ginger. Ylang-ylang also makes the cut: “Something about it is so ’90s perfume coded. It feels very solar and fiery to me.” 

Next up are the earth signs — Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn — whose grounded, no-nonsense energy calls for equally distinctive notes. “There’s like a control and unyieldingness,” Grant says. Think bold, specific scents with a strong point of view. For her, that means vetiver. Kelly is very much in agreement, noting, “It’s because it’s such a straightforward note. What you see is what you get. Yes. It’s like there’s not really that much wiggle room with a vetiver.” Translation: If you’re an earth sign, your fragrance doesn’t need to do the most to make an impression. 

Then come the air signs — Aquarius, Gemini, and Libra — the zodiac’s more whimsical, cerebral bunch. Grant, a double Aquarius, gushes about one of her all-time favorite notes: jasmine. “But it is the scent that is a little itty-bitty cute white little flower. So intense, almost narcotic-like, goes into your nose, passages into your brain and, like, sticks there to the point where you can’t think about anything else.” In other words, never underestimate the power of a tiny flower with main-character energy. 

Last but not least, the water signs — Pisces, Scorpio, and Cancer — bring a more intuitive, emotional sensibility to the fragrance conversation. Amber is one standout, with Kelly describing it as “very soft, plush, warm, cozy.” It’s an enveloping kind of scent, perfect for anyone who wants their fragrance to feel less like an accessory and more like a comforting second skin. 

Of course, the stars aren’t the only inspiration behind this episode. Throughout the conversation, Grant and Kelly also explore the EOS holiday collection, which features three brand-new, highly giftable scents. Kelly even offers a fragrance forecast for each one, sharing what their signature notes might have in store for the year ahead. 

DashDividers_1_500x100

First up is Cotton Candy Fleur, with notes of strawberry spun sugar, orange blossom, magnolia, patchouli, and midnight woods. Its forecast? Creativity. “This smells like creativity,” Kelly predicts. “This is for budding artists in 2027. This is for songwriters, musicians, people who want to be seen and heard.” Consider it a little olfactory inspiration for anyone ready to put their ideas out into the world. 

Next, there’s Cozy Comfort, a plush blend of sueded vanilla, creamy amaretto, sheer skin-like musk, and mahogany woods. Its power word is romance. “It’s giving really nice faux fur blanket, like wrapped up nuzzling. It’s giving engagement. Under the tree,” Kelly says. Whether you’re manifesting a holiday proposal or simply craving a little more softness in your life, this scent is all about leaning into love. 

Finally, Frosted Plum & Amber is what we can only imagine the Nutcracker’s Sugar Plum Fairy smells like. But beyond its festive sweetness, Kelly sees a scent synonymous with abundance and knowing your worth. “She knows her worth and is not afraid to walk away from a bad negotiation because she knows she’s valuable. And then everyone on the other side of the table is like, ‘Well, give her whatever she wants.’” Honestly, that’s the kind of energy we’re bringing into 2027. 

Whether you’re looking to find your zodiac’s signature notes, manifest a little romance, or channel your most confident self in the new year, this Nose Dive finale makes a compelling case for letting fragrance be part of the ritual. After all, the right scent doesn’t just smell good — it can help you step into the version of yourself you’re ready to become.

title: Louisa Jacobson’s Message To The Gilded Age Fans Rooting For Marian & Larry: “I Hear You. I Get It.”
text:
Louisa Jacobson’s Message To The Gilded Age Fans Rooting For Marian & Larry: “I Hear You. I Get It.”

Spoilers for The Gilded Age Season 4 ahead. Marian Brook and Larry Russell did something scandalous in the season premiere of The Gilded Age, and now they are facing the fallout. In Episode 2, which aired last night, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) is panicked and cloaked in shame after she and Larry (Harry Richardson) spent the night together… in the biblical sense. They had sex. Gasp! To Marian, it really is that serious. She is worried that their act could put her at risk of social ruin and she’s not wrong. For Larry, hooking up with Marian is the perfect “excuse” to marry her. Yeah, that comment went over just as well as you’d imagine. By the end of the episode, Marian is still riddled with regret and Larry is left lovesick and confused. Of course, the discourse has ignited the Gilded Age fandom (specifically, #Larian shippers) and fans have been quick to share their frustration with Marian. But Louisa Jacobson says it’s time to show her character some grace. 

“ The main message I have for the fans is that you guys have to remember the time period that we are living in in the Gilded Age,” Jacobson tells me during the show’s press junket in New York, flanked by co-stars, Richardson, Ben Ahlers (Jack Trotter), and Denée Benton (Peggy Scott). “ Marian is an example of 19th century Victorian ideals, purity, modesty, and morality. Premarital sex is a cardinal sin [and] women had no access to education about their sexual health, about their bodies.” Jacobson is animated and passionate in her defense of her character, but she also makes it clear that this storyline is not one she would have chosen. 

“ We’re not writing this,” Jacobson says frankly. “We are given it, and we have to stand by it, own it, and make it ours [but] it can be really, really hard to do.” She also admits to paying attention to the online response to Marian’s choices and let’s just say that fans haven’t been easy on the character. “You asked if we are online following what people are saying, and I am for better or for worse, honestly…  It’s easy to get caught up in what you think other people think is wrong with your character. I understand [but] I think I’ve tried to shed this need to please a lot of people who just won’t be pleased.” 

It surprises me that Jacobson admits to being tapped into the online discourse, because she’s no stranger to fame (her mother is Meryl Streep and her sisters, Mamie and Grace Gummer, are also actors), but it’s refreshing to hear her candor about how the backlash has affected her. And I think everyone needs to calm down with their criticism of the character.

Marian has made her share of confounding decisions (remember when she gifted Peggy dirty old shoes because she assumed she was poor? The same Peggy who loaned her broke ass bus money? I digress.) but in this case, I think people are being too harsh. Marian’s reputation is on the line. Larry can go to as many brothels as he chooses, get tagged as a rake or a playboy, and he still gets to carry on being a respected businessman and heir to the Russell fortune. Marian would bring shame upon her family (hasn’t Aunt Agnes suffered enough?) and soil her chances of marriage altogether if anyone found out about their little rendezvous. 

 ”It was a very, very different world that they lived in, and they had a very different relationship [sex],” Jacobson continues. “It’s easy to forget when there’s all these wonderful other rich storylines that have glimmers to them that feel very modern in their struggles, but this one is very, very rooted in its period.”  

Jacobson brings up a great point, and the accuracy to its time period is why we love The Gilded Age. Yes, so many storylines are current-day, real-world parallels (like George Russell’s fight against anti-monopoly laws or Peggy’s mother-in-law’s respectability politics), but in this case, Marian is acting exactly as a woman of her time and stature would. It would be unrealistic and against character to make Marian Brook be chill about having sex with Larry Russell. Of all the things Marian is (intelligent, selfless, compassionate, stubborn, righteous, a little annoying), she is not nonchalant. Of course, she is freaking out. But I think it’s important to let the storyline play out as the season unfolds. In Sonja Warfield we trust. 

Harry Richardson didn’t have much to say in defense of Larry (although, the character should be getting a bit more flack — the man could be more understanding of Marian’s meltdown!), but he did have one thing to say to fans: “Hang in there.” Ahlers, who was giving the energy of a #Larian shipper himself, added: “Hang in there! It’s a really beautiful story.”

title: Is Wicker Worth Watching? Our Honest Review Of The Horny Feminist Film
text:
Is Wicker Worth Watching? Our Honest Review Of The Horny Feminist Film

The romantic fantasy comedy Wicker is now in theaters, but is it worth watching? From the trailer, it looks like a horny, sex-filled romp between Olivia Colman, who plays the Fisherwoman, and Alexander Skarsgård, the Wicker Husband. And while it may begin that way, there are deeper themes of feminism, toxic masculinity and the way women are treated in society woven throughout.

At first, we meet the Fisherwoman. She’s tired of being an outcast in her Medieval village due to her stench and unmarried status, so she commissions a Wicker Husband from the Basket Weaver. The new couple become the envy of the women in the town, not for their passionate sex (of which there’s a lot), but for how caring, helpful and sweet the Wicker Husband is towards his wife.

So, is Wicker worth watching? Entertainment writers Rebekah Manibog and Rachel Choy sat down to discuss the juicy details, whether you see the Dicker (AKA the Wicker Husband’s… parts), and how terrifying the parallels are to modern life. Mild spoilers follow.

Rachel Choy: Wicker is probably one of my favorite movies this year. I actually really, really loved it.

Rebekah Manibog: Me too.

RC: I didn’t expect to like it this much. I thought it would be fun; I like Olivia Colman. I wasn’t frothing over the Wicker Husband like everybody else online, and was surprised it was such a cute and wholesome love story.

RM: I think what I also find really funny is that everyone is obviously going off the trailer, and that really amps up the horniness. But when you actually watch the movie, it’s a bigger picture of the patriarchy and also how society sees single women.

RC: And single older women.

RM: And also a wife’s place. If you notice all the characters’ names, they don’t have names. It’s their husband’s job, and then plus wife.

RC: For example, The Baker’s Wife, The Tailor’s Wife. But it’s interesting that Olivia Colman’s character is called the Fisherwoman. She has her own job. She’s actually progressive! And it’s set in a sort of Medieval era, but weirdly, there are a lot of things that relate to the modern era. The whole Tradwife movement is happening now, and it’s very similar to the values in this movie. The men run the house, the women do whatever the men want, and they stay home and look after the man. The men don’t care about satisfying their wives. They don’t care about their wife’s happiness. This feels too close to home.

RM: There’s so much commentary now about how shit the dating pool is. As a single woman in Sydney, I cannot escape the amount of horror stories, or like how chivalry is dead and all that. And I definitely noticed even though it was set in a medieval time, there are a lot of parallels to now.

RC: In saying that, there is still some horniness.

RM: Oh, a lot of horniness. I like how they kind of got it out of the way.

RC: Yes! He gets created, and then instantly they’re having sex, breaking the bed, and every time he moves, he’s creaking. But you don’t get a close up of his dicker.

RM: You see it from far away.

RC: I’m guessing it’s not hard.

RM: It’s implied that it’s huge, because the sound they make when they look down, and it’s huge, and apparently it’s erect. I don’t know what that looks like. I’m a child of God!

RC: And he does have nipples.

RM: Yes, he does, which Alexander Skarsgård has spoken about a lot during his press tour.

RC: And he told you about the nipples specifically.

RM: He told me about the nipples in my interview with him, and he also gifted nipples. They were also talking about letting people win nipples as well. That was fun!

RC: So it’s still sexy, but then it’s also really heartwarming. And the Wicker Husband is such a caring, perfect man. He’s everything that you would want. He’s sensitive. He does things before he’s told. He fixes the roof. He does the chores.

RM: He helps his wife, and all the other women are like, “Oh, that’s actually really sexy.”

RC: Yeah, and then the men are like, “Oh shit.”

RM: What I also find nice as well is that they’re not initially attracted to his physical being. They’re attracted because he dances with her. One of the other wives wanted to dance with him, and that’s what kind of made everyone a yearnalist, basically, because it’s the way that he treated Olivia Colman, the Fisherwoman. It wasn’t just based off him being hot.

RC: And then you see their relationship grow through the mundane things, and there’s a whole lot of other stuff that develops. There’s a major spoiler we won’t go into, but there’s a really creepy thing that happens. I feel like it’ll leave you with a lot to think about. About how women are treated, both in relationships and as single women, because the ones in relationships aren’t treated well either. It pretty much just sucks to be a woman. Yeah, and when you think about toxic masculinity, what that does and how that ruins relationships. And also women that uphold the patriarchy. The Tailor’s Wife really upholds it and is threatened by anything that will disturb the current status quo.

RM: She resents it because she’s stuck in there. She’s kind of also the monarch, I would say, of the village.

RC: It’s what Olivia Rodrigo says in her song, If they do it to them, they’ll do it to you. You might be the cream of the crop of the women, or whatever, but you’re still at the bottom of the pile when it comes to men. So shouldn’t you all get together and revolt?

RM: And it’s also shown in that scene when the Tailor’s Wife sews a man up after an accident. But the male town doctor is thanked, not her. And also, it’s very on the nose, the first bride we see wears a collar.

RC: Oh my god, yes, the collar around her neck! They’re like animals.

RM: Exactly, and the fisherwoman was the only one who didn’t wear a collar at her wedding. And then look, she’s in the best relationship.

RC: I feel it’s a film that we can learn from. I think people should watch it, even if they’re just watching it for the horniness. You’ll also get something else out of it. And if you think it’s weird that people are falling in love with a wicker man, there’s more to the movie than that. I think it’s worth watching. I really loved it.

RM: I think so, especially if you are an older single lady.

RC: Or in a toxic relationship. It might make you think.

RM: Oh, and please don’t try anything with wicker.

RC: Yeah, don’t insert that. Even though wood gets bigger when it’s wet.

RM: Oh my god, does it?

RC: It expands. I’ll leave you with that.

This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Wicker is now in theaters.

title: Everything We Know About Heated Rivalry Season 2 & 3 (And A Movie!?)
text:
Everything We Know About Heated Rivalry Season 2 & 3 (And A Movie!?)

We are heading to the cottage for Heated Rivalry Season 2, Season 3 and even a movie! The Crave Canada turned HBO Max smash hit was renewed for a second season after becoming extremely popular, with Connor Storrie returning as Ilya Rozanov and Hudson Williams as Shane Hollander. After it was picked up by HBO, the queer hockey romance had audiences swooning all around the world. It kick-started both young actors’ careers, who went on to present an award at the Golden Globes. To put it simply, Williams, Storrie and Heated Rivalry have become global phenomenons.

We’ve rounded up everything you need to know about Heated Rivalry Season 2, including the potential release date, what the showrunner has teased, the plot and more. Plus, there’s some more information about Season 3 and the movie. Grab your hockey stick, it’s time to hit the ice.

When will Heated Rivalry Season 2 be released?

According to Deadline, Heated Rivalry Season 2 will be released around April 2027.

What do we know about Heated Rivalry Season 3 and the movie?

Deadline claims that Season 2 and Season 3 are being filmed back-to-back, and will wrap at the end of November or at the start of December. The movie will center around Scott and Kip, played by Francois Arnaud and Robbie G.K., but Ilya and Shane will not make an appearance. It’s said to be a Christmas special or holiday-themed.

What is the plot of Heated Rivalry Season 2?

Heated Rivalry Season 2 will be based on Rachel Reid’s books The Long Game and Role Model.

In The Long Game book, Ilya and Shane are still mostly a closeted couple, apart from a handful of friends and Shane’s family members. While Shane is now out and proud to his teammates, Ilya has to stay in the closet to keep their romance a secret. It wears on him, and the couple start to face some real challenges.

Role Model focuses on Troy Barrett, a closeted gay player for Ottawa. He’s mentored by Ilya and Wyatt Hayes, and starts to get close to openly out social media manager Harris Drover. Perhaps Troy and Harris will have their own standalone episode!

Where can you watch Heated Rivalry Season 2?

Heated Rivalry Season 2 will be streaming on HBO Max. While you wait for the next season to drop, you can rewatch Heated Rivalry Season 1.

What has the showrunner said about Heated Rivalry Season 2?

Showrunner Jacob Tierney is back for Heated Rivalry Season 2 and has written the script. During a panel at BookCon in New York, he said this season will delve into “serious territory” when it comes to Shane and Ilya’s relationship.

“A lot of the initial — there’s still lots of flirting and lots of sex — but this kind of danger, this kind of hotel-room-adolescent-sex stuff is largely gone. And so it presents really new challenges,” Tierney said. “Obviously, parts of Role Model are going to be in [Season 2], to the great surprise of absolutely nobody. But Ilya and Shane are the heartbeat of this series, of my show. It’s always going to be about Ilya and Shane, that is what is the trajectory that runs through it as their world expands.”

title: Your Horoscope This Week: November 8 To 14
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: November 8 To 14

Cosmic beings, this may be the most exciting week of November, and after weeks of retrograde reflection, the cosmos is finally giving us something to celebrate! The week begins with a powerful Scorpio New Moon in the early hours of November 9th, kick-starting a six-month chapter of profound transformation and renewal. This is one of the most emotionally significant New Moons of the year, inviting us to get radically honest about what we’re ready to change and who we’re becoming in the process. With Scorpio’s traditional ruler Mars in passionate Leo and its modern ruler Pluto in innovative Aquarius, there’s a fiery, intellectual edge to this lunation that encourages us to blend intuition with action. The intentions we set over the next ten days could deeply influence the direction of the next six months, so dream boldly, own your power, and be willing to take the first steps toward what you want.

Then, on November 13th, we receive a double cosmic blessing as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends its retrograde in Libra. Hallelujah! After weeks of crossed wires, relationship revelations, financial delays, and perhaps a few unsolicited trips down memory lane, we can finally start making sense of everything we’ve experienced. Mercury retrograde may have exposed conversations we needed to revisit or truths we’d been avoiding, while Venus retrograde pushed us to reconsider what we value, how we love, and where our energy is being reciprocated. Now, with Mercury moving forward in Scorpio and Venus moving forward in Libra, we can use those insights to make clearer decisions, repair connections where there’s mutual willingness, and move on from situations that have run their course. We’ve spent weeks figuring out what needs to change. Now we get to do something about it.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, your next financial breakthrough could come from thinking beyond what you can accomplish on your own. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your investments and wealth-building realm, opening a six-month chapter of financial transformation. You may feel inspired to explore a business partnership, apply for funding, or develop a strategy for creating long-term financial security. With your ruling planet Mars in Leo energizing your creativity, an idea you’re passionate about could become an unexpected source of income. Think about the resources, expertise, or support you could leverage to bring your vision to life. There’s power in knowing when to collaborate, Aries.

On November 13th, Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping you make progress with financial applications, contracts, or negotiations that have required extra patience. You may finally receive information about an investment, insurance matter, or shared financial obligation that’s been difficult to sort out. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra brings renewed momentum to your partnership realm. If you’ve been reconsidering a romantic or professional commitment, you may feel more confident about what you want moving forward. The second half of November could be especially promising for agreements that benefit everyone involved, so pay attention to who shares your vision.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, two heads may be better than one, especially when it comes to your biggest ambitions. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your partnership and collaboration zone, launching a six-month chapter that could introduce important new alliances into your life. Perhaps you’re ready to find a business partner, work with a mentor, or team up with someone whose skills complement your own. With Mars in Leo energizing your home and family realm, you may also be considering a joint investment in property or a project involving relatives. Think about what you could create with the right person by your side, Taurus. An exciting partnership could open doors you hadn’t previously considered.

Then November 13th brings a welcome turning point as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping you finalize agreements, revisit proposals, or clarify expectations with someone you’re working closely with. A connection that seemed uncertain may finally start taking shape. Your ruling planet Venus also ends its retrograde in Libra, bringing fresh energy to your work, wellness, and daily-routine realm. If you’ve been questioning your professional environment or how much time you’re dedicating to other people’s priorities, you may feel ready to make some changes. Your schedule should leave room for your own ambitions, Taurus, and this is a promising time to create that balance.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, what if your next career breakthrough came from completely reimagining how you work? The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your productivity and wellness realm, launching a six-month chapter of professional and lifestyle improvements. You may feel inspired to transition into a new role, develop a specialized skill, or explore technology that could make your work more efficient. With Mars in Leo energizing your communication and learning zone, opportunities involving writing, teaching, marketing, or digital media could be especially appealing. Think about what your ideal workday would look like and which changes could bring you closer to experiencing it.

On November 13th, your ruling planet Mercury finally ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping you move forward with job applications, workplace negotiations, or projects that have been stuck in revision mode. You may receive useful feedback from a supervisor or discover a more effective way to manage your responsibilities. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra brings a refreshing boost to your creativity, pleasure, and self-expression zone. A hobby or artistic project you’ve neglected could suddenly feel exciting again, and you may even discover an opportunity to share it with a wider audience. There’s room for both professional success and personal enjoyment in your next chapter, Gemini. Make space for both.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, that creative idea you’ve been sitting on deserves a bigger stage. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your creativity, fame, fate, and self-expression zone, opening a six-month chapter where your talents could take you further than you imagined. Whether you’ve been considering launching a passion project, sharing your work publicly, or turning a hobby into a business, this lunation encourages you to take your gifts seriously. With Mars in Leo energizing your income realm, there’s also potential to connect your creativity with greater financial independence. Think about what you’d love to have created or accomplished by next spring, and give yourself permission to be ambitious about it.

On November 13th, Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, making it easier to pitch ideas, revisit creative collaborations, or finally get feedback on something you’ve been developing. A project that lost momentum could find its spark again. Meanwhile, Venus ends its retrograde in Libra, bringing greater clarity to home and family matters. If you’ve been weighing a move, negotiating household arrangements, or trying to make your living environment more comfortable, you may feel ready to settle on a direction. Your private life and creative ambitions can support each other, Cancer, and this week helps you figure out how.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, your home may be ready for an upgrade, and we’re talking about more than a new couch. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th begins a six-month chapter of transformation involving your living situation, family, and sense of belonging. You could be preparing to relocate, considering homeownership, or thinking seriously about how you want your household to function. With Mars in your sign, you’re feeling more motivated to take charge of these decisions, while Pluto in Aquarius brings important questions about partnership and shared responsibilities into the picture. What kind of home would make your everyday life easier, happier, and more aligned with your future plans?

Then November 13th brings relief as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping stalled housing decisions, family logistics, or property-related paperwork move forward. You may finally receive information that makes your next steps easier to plan. Venus also ends its retrograde in Libra, bringing renewed momentum to your communication, learning, and immediate environment. An application, writing project, or conversation you’ve been revisiting could start gaining traction. You may also feel more inspired to explore your neighborhood or connect with people who can oﬀer useful advice. Sometimes the right information arrives just when you’re ready to put it to use, Leo.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, you could be sitting on an idea that’s worth sharing with a much bigger audience. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your communication, writing, and learning realm, opening a six-month chapter of intellectual growth. Perhaps you’re ready to launch a newsletter, start a podcast, learn a language, or develop an expertise that could open professional doors. With Mars in Leo moving through your behind-the-scenes zone, some of your best work may begin privately, while you’re researching, experimenting, and figuring out what you want to say. You have time to develop your voice, but don’t underestimate how far one well-executed idea could take you.

On November 13th, your ruling planet Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping you move forward with submissions, presentations, contracts, or educational plans that have required multiple revisions. You may finally feel ready to send something out into the world after weeks of fine-tuning it. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra brings welcome clarity to your finances and earning potential. If you’ve been reconsidering your pricing, negotiating payment, or evaluating the financial value of a skill, you could feel better equipped to advocate for yourself. Your knowledge has value, and the second half of November is a good time to start treating it that way.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, what if the next six months completely transformed your relationship with money and your sense of self-worth? The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your income, security, and abundance zone, encouraging you to set intentions around the kind of financial freedom you want to create. With Mars in Leo energizing your friendship and future-goals realm, a collaboration or connection within your network could help you see new possibilities for building wealth. Think about what you want your financial life to look like by next spring, including how much you want to earn, save, or invest. The more specific you get about your goals, the easier it’ll be to recognize opportunities that can help you achieve them.

Then November 13th brings a major turning point as your ruling planet Venus finally ends its retrograde in your sign, alongside Mercury ending its retrograde in Scorpio. If the past several weeks have felt like one long identity crisis, you may be more than ready to come up for air! Venus direct can help restore your confidence in your appearance, relationships, and personal direction, especially if you’ve been questioning decisions you once felt certain about. Meanwhile, Mercury direct in your financial realm could bring clarity to delayed payments, negotiations, or important money conversations. Give yourself credit for the ways you’ve grown through this retrograde season, Libra. You’re entering the second half of November with a stronger sense of who you are and what you’re worth.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, your solar return season’s getting increasingly better. Your annual New Moon arrives on November 9th, and this one has “fresh start” written all over it. Think of yourself as emerging from a chrysalis, with the next six months offering you the chance to spread your wings in ways you may have only dreamed about until now. This New Moon in your sign is ideal for setting intentions around your identity, confidence, appearance, and the experiences you want to invite into your life. With Mars in Leo activating your career and public-image realm and Pluto in Aquarius transforming your home and family zone, you may feel inspired to reinvent both your public persona and your private world. Let yourself get excited about what’s possible, Scorpio. You’ve done plenty of reflecting lately, and now you get to start creating.

Then November 13th brings another reason to celebrate as Mercury finally ends its retrograde in your sign, while Venus ends hers in Libra. Mercury direct can help you regain momentum with personal projects, important decisions, or conversations you’ve been postponing. You may find that people are more receptive to your ideas or that expressing yourself feels easier after weeks of second-guessing. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your solitude and spirituality realm could bring a welcome sense of inner peace, especially if you’ve been processing complicated feelings about someone from your past. You may realize that a situation you once obsessed over simply doesn’t occupy as much space in your mind anymore. Enjoy that freedom, Scorpio. Your birthday season deserves to feel like a celebration of everything you’re becoming.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sag, what if some of your biggest breakthroughs over the next six months happen when nobody’s watching? The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your solitude, spirituality, and behind-the-scenes realm, making this a powerful time to nurture ideas that aren’t quite ready for the spotlight. You may feel inspired to work privately on a creative project, explore a spiritual practice, or make plans for a personal reinvention that you’ll reveal when the timing feels right. With Mars in fellow Fire sign Leo energizing your travel and expansion zone, your imagination may be running wild with possibilities. Give yourself permission to experiment without needing immediate feedback or approval.

On November 13th, Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping you gain clarity about plans or decisions you’ve been considering. You may finally connect the dots on an idea that seemed too complicated a few weeks ago or find a more practical way to bring it to life. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra brings renewed energy to your friendships, collaborations, and social life. An invitation, introduction, or opportunity to reconnect with someone could lead to something promising, especially if you’ve been craving more inspiring company. With your birthday season beginning next week, Sag, you may feel your enthusiasm returning in full force. Enjoy the anticipation, and start making room in your calendar for the adventures ahead.

Capricorn Sun & Rising:

Capricorn, what if the right people could help you accomplish in six months what you’ve been trying to do alone for years? The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th activates your friendship, community, and future-goals realm, opening a powerful chapter for collaboration and collective success. You may feel inspired to join an organization, build a stronger professional network, or turn a shared vision into something tangible. With Mars in Leo energizing your shared-resources zone, conversations about funding, investments, or pooling resources could become especially relevant. Think about the kind of support system your next big goal actually requires, and be willing to let others contribute.

On November 13th, Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, making it easier to coordinate group projects, finalize plans with collaborators, or reconnect with contacts who went quiet. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra brings welcome momentum to your career and public image. A professional relationship that felt strained may improve, or you could gain a clearer understanding of how to position yourself for an opportunity you’ve been pursuing. You may find that someone who previously overlooked your work is suddenly paying attention. Stay open to conversations that could lead somewhere promising.

Aquarius Sun & Rising:

Aquarius, your next career move could change how people see you, and more importantly, how you see yourself. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th illuminates your career, reputation, and legacy zone, launching a six-month period of professional reinvention. You may feel ready to pursue a leadership position, launch a business, or take your expertise into an entirely new field. With Mars in Leo activating your partnership realm, an important collaborator, client, or romantic partner could influence the direction you choose. This is a powerful moment to consider what you want your name associated with and which opportunities deserve your full commitment.

Then November 13th brings relief as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, helping stalled professional negotiations, applications, or decisions involving authority figures gain traction. If you’ve been waiting for feedback or clarification about a project, you may finally get some answers. Venus also ends its retrograde in Libra, bringing fresh perspective to your travel, education, and publishing realm. A delayed trip, academic application, or international opportunity could become easier to navigate. You may realize that expanding your skills or exploring a different environment is exactly what your professional growth requires.

Pisces Sun & Rising:

Pisces, your world is about to get bigger, and the Scorpio New Moon on November 9th wants you to be intentional about where you go next. This lunation activates your travel, publishing, and spiritual expansion zone, opening a six-month chapter of discovery. Perhaps you’re considering relocating, pursuing a qualification, sharing your work with a wider audience, or exploring a culture that’s always fascinated you. With Mars in Leo energizing your daily-routine realm, the challenge is finding practical ways to make room for these experiences. Start researching the logistics, costs, and commitments involved. A dream becomes much more exciting when you can see a realistic path toward it.

On November 13th, Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, bringing greater clarity to travel arrangements, educational paperwork, or publishing matters that have been delayed. You may receive news from someone abroad or finally feel ready to commit to a direction you’ve been researching. Meanwhile, Venus direct in Libra helps untangle questions involving shared finances, loans, or financial support from others. If money has been a deciding factor in your plans, you may have a better understanding of what’s available and what still needs to be arranged. There’s plenty to look forward to, Pisces, and this week can help you move from possibility to preparation.
